items.title: Randy Weston — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Melba Liston did all the arrangements, by the way.

ctx.x: That experience of doing “Earth Birth” with the strings, and I’m happy to say I was there, but that experience was part of a larger residency that you did at the Montreal Jazz Festival that year. Talk about that residency and what you did.

It was incredible. I hope I can remember everything correctly, but they gave me five nights. The first night was a duo with myself and David Murray. And the next night, not necessarily in that order, I did a concert with the Gnawa musicians of Morocco with a band which consisted of TK Blue, Teddy Edwards, Benny Powell, Alex Blake, Neil Clarke…I cant remember the names of all the musicians. Anyhow, that was like the African night, okay? Melba Liston did all the arrangements, by the way. The next time we did the…

items.title: Melba Liston — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: And I wrote them. I think it’s the best thing. Quite nice. It’s the best thing. I’m on it.

ctx.x: Oh yeah. I hear of everybody. I didn’t expect to see him or to write for him or anything like that. He said, “Can I bring some lead sheets up to your house and you make them for me?” I said okay. He brought Little Niles and all those things up to the house, and he said, “I think you should write these things for an album for me.” And I wrote them. I think it’s the best thing. Quite nice. It’s the best thing. I’m on it. Johnny Griffin, and Ray Copeland. And he and probably Charli Persip – can’t think of the bass…
I haven’t heard it in so long. Did they re-release it?
